intro: We hold a recorded main-programme fee of up to ₹{{budget}} lakh for {{count}} published Integrated Law colleges in India. This list of the best Integrated Law colleges under ₹{{budget}} lakh should be read as a fee filter for five-year programmes such as BA LLB.

DS College, Aligarh, is listed first with BA LLB at ₹10,060, which is only just above our ₹10,000 data floor. A figure that low for a five-year course is often an annual tuition, so confirm the official total.
Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Punjab have the most listings. CLAT and LAWCET are the main recorded entrance tests.
listLead: These are the top Integrated Law colleges in India 2026 with a recorded main-programme fee of up to ₹1 lakh. The first cards include BA LLB and a Bachelor of Socio Legal Sciences LL.B., which are related but not identical awards.
snapshot: Across {{feeN}} published colleges with a recorded fee, the median total is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half sits between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}.
{{private}} colleges are private, {{public}} are public, and a few have no ownership type. Bangalore, Bhopal and Jalandhar are the leading cities on this list.
Two records have a fee band that can exceed ₹1 lakh. Use the official five-year fee, not only the first-year number, when you budget.
firstCollegesLead: MS Ramaiah Law College, Bangalore, is listed with BA LLB at ₹16,000, and Adarsha Law College, Warangal, at ₹18,000–₹21,000. Both figures look like annual amounts unless the official notice says otherwise.
PES Modern Law College, Pune, is listed with B.S.L. LL.B. at ₹22,000 and a 2023 average package of ₹6 lakh. That placement figure is historical and may not be for every integrated-law batch.

sections.heading: Five-year law fees and entrance tests
paragraphs: A five-year integrated law fee is easy to understate if our record stores one year. Multiply only when the official notice is clearly annual, and never invent the missing years.
CLAT is recorded at six colleges here, and LAWCET at five. Many private colleges also run a separate institute process.

compare.heading: How to compare the best Integrated Law colleges under ₹1 lakh
paragraphs: A university BA LLB and a private five-year programme can share this cap and still differ in affiliation, clerkship exposure and official yearly fees.
bullets: Whether the recorded fee is for one year or the full five years, plus exam and enrolment charges.
The official award, such as BA LLB, BBA LLB or B.S.L. LL.B.
The admission test, including CLAT, LAWCET, MH CET Law, or a university process.
Bar Council of India approval and the university affiliation named on the official site.

faqs.question: How many integrated law colleges have fees under ₹1 lakh here?
faqs.answer: We list {{published}} published Integrated Law colleges with a recorded main-programme fee up to ₹{{budget}} lakh. Colleges without a usable fee on file are excluded.

faqs.question: What is a typical integrated law fee on this list?
faqs.answer: The median recorded total is {{feeMedian}}, and the middle half falls between {{feeP25}} and {{feeP75}}. For a five-year course, confirm whether the official notice is annual.

faqs.question: Why is the first college fee only about ₹10,000?
faqs.answer: DS College, Aligarh, is listed with BA LLB at ₹10,060, just above the ₹10,000 floor we treat as a data error. Confirm the official five-year or annual fee before you treat it as the complete cost.

faqs.question: Do these colleges admit through CLAT?
faqs.answer: CLAT is recorded at six colleges on this list, and LAWCET at five. Many others use a state or university test. Check the official admission page.

faqs.question: Is this a ranking of the best Integrated Law colleges under ₹1 lakh?
faqs.answer: No. It is a fee filter. Affiliation, approval and the official five-year fee should guide the shortlist, not the recorded number alone.
